title: Coefficient Chern comparison for a finite geometrically normalized Cartier class
statement: Let prime l and Y satisfy the noetherian and invertibility hypotheses above. Let c be Chern data satisfying c.Normalized [def-sp-tower-class-chern] and FiniteChernNormalization [def-sp-tower-class-finite], r a scalar restriction, k its normalized coefficient cones [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-coefficients], n≥0, a a normalized finite frame [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-finite-boundary-frame] and L any derived-limit model. For any residue-coefficient supported Cartier class z satisfying GeoCartierChernEquation for the diagonal [def-sfb-geo-cartier-interface], a.cartierMap(L,z) [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-finite-boundary-cartier-map] equals finiteChernComposite(L,n,diagonalPic(Y)) [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-finite-chern-composite]. There is no strict class xi, reduction D, source cone s or Ext presentation p in this statement. The Picard class diagonalPic is the dual diagonal ideal [def-sp-tower-class-diagonal].

source.place: paragraph (2), finite Cartier normalization and forget supports, before the divisor line is decomposed; diagonal-limit clause (3), and classes proof (3)

proof.text: Apply FiniteChernNormalization to diagonalPic(Y) and n. Use c.Normalized to identify the actual positive Kummer boundary and scalar comparisons. Unpack the geometric Chern equation for z to obtain an etale finite class with integral adjunct the supported Kummer Chern class and whose site pullback is the forget-support composite of z. The diagonal Picard line is the dual diagonal ideal.

The coefficient-one and root-tensor equations of k and the two frame normalizations identify the finite quotient and root endpoint maps in the normalization equation with the ordinary finite ones. Use scalar_unit_ext_bijective for the integral generator of the finite constant module to recover equality of the finite coefficient-linear arrows from their integral adjuncts. Transport through the canonical exact single, shift, evaluation and restriction maps and precompose the coefficient projection. The exact-cone projection identity gives k.unitMap followed by L.projection n, hence the stated equality.
